Direct mapping; also the building block for cart-abandonment segments.
Straightforward to add, but needs a name and owner agreed so it isn't duplicated later.
Logic that used to live in Processing Rules moves upstream into Data Prep at ingestion; this is a rebuild, not a copy.

mapping.target: Lookup dataset joined via Data Prep, or schema field enrichment
mapping.why: SAINT classifications don't migrate automatically; they become a lookup dataset or a richer upstream field.
CJA adds a Person container, so most AA visitor-scoped segments become simpler and more accurate as Person-scoped segments.

mapping.target: Derived Fields / Calculated Metrics in Data View

Conceptually similar; needs to be reconfigured against the new metrics once parity is reached.

questions.title: How many of these do you have?
questions.help: Here's how each selected element maps into CJA / XDM, and what it takes to get there.

questions.title: Flag the ones worth rebuilding

options.label: Started, didn't finish
options.description: People who added something to their cart but never completed the purchase.
options.note: Person container in CJA evaluates this across every channel and device tied to that identity, not just the session or browser where the cart add happened.

options.label: High-value / high-loyalty customers
options.description: Your best customers, measured by how much they've bought or how loyal they've been.
options.note: Person container aggregates every identity (web, app, in-person/CRM) into one lifetime view, so the threshold reflects the whole relationship, not one device's slice of it.

options.label: Multi-channel engaged
options.description: People who interact with you across more than one channel or device.
options.note: Native cross-dataset, cross-channel sequencing once identities are stitched: no add-on required, and it's auditable at the event level.

options.label: Engaged with content, didn't convert
options.description: People who read, watched, or browsed content but took no further action.
options.note: Same logic, but can span visits and channels via the Person container, catching converters who came back on a different device.

options.label: Churn / lapse risk
options.description: Customers whose activity has dropped off compared to their usual pattern.
options.note: Same pattern, but can be paired with a Derived Field for recency and refreshed automatically; often layered with Intelligent Alerts.

options.label: Campaign responders
options.description: People who clicked, opened, or otherwise responded to a specific campaign.
options.note: Same idea, strengthened by Attribution IQ so response can be credited across every touch, not just last-touch.

options.label: Recent service / support interaction
options.description: Customers who've recently contacted support or opened a service case.
options.note: A joinable dataset (e.g. CRM case data) becomes just another event stream in the Person container: a genuinely new capability for most AA implementations.

options.label: New vs. returning
options.description: Distinguishes first-time visitors from people who've been here before.
options.note: Same logic, made more reliable because 'returning' is evaluated against the full stitched identity rather than a device-scoped visitor ID.

questions.title: Sort each control
questions.help: Assign a status to as many controls as apply - each one is independent, so more than one can be "In place."

options.label: Data Governance Labels
options.description: Sensitivity labels (e.g. contractual, identity-linked, sensitive) applied to fields in the schema.
options.note: A field holding health or financial sensitivity is labeled at the schema level, and that label travels with the data everywhere it's used.

options.label: Access Control Groups / Sandboxes
options.description: Who can see which datasets, Data Views and sandboxes.
options.note: A regional marketing team gets access to their sandbox and Data Views only, separate from the global analytics team's production sandbox.

options.label: Data Usage Labels
options.description: Contractual or legal restrictions on how specific data can be used downstream (e.g. no use in targeted advertising).
options.note: A dataset sourced under a contract that prohibits ad-targeting use carries a usage label that blocks it from activation flows.

options.label: Consent & Identity Governance
options.description: Opt-outs and consent preferences propagate to every identity tied to a person, not just one dataset.
options.note: A customer opts out on the website; that preference is honored across app, email and offline touchpoints because it's tied to the identity graph.

fields.text: CJA Workspace with cross-channel Data Views, plus Query Service for SQL-level access to raw event data.

fields.label: New skill to build
fields.text: Thinking in Person vs. Event vs. Session containers, and when to use each.

fields.label: Quick win
fields.text: The first rebuilt Data View usually answers a cross-channel question that was previously impossible, a good moment to demonstrate value early.

fields.label: Moving from
fields.text: Segments built and used inside Adobe Analytics, manually exported for activation.

fields.label: Moving to
fields.text: Segments built in CJA, activated directly into Real-Time CDP / Journey Optimizer without manual export.

fields.label: New skill to build
fields.text: Understanding that a Person-container segment already reflects every channel: no more stitching audiences by hand across tools.

fields.label: Quick win
fields.text: Show a segment triggering an actual message send in the same workshop; the previously multi-day activation process becomes minutes.

fields.label: Moving from
fields.text: s.tags / AppMeasurement, Processing Rules, SAINT classifications.

fields.label: Moving to
fields.text: Web/Mobile SDK on Edge Network, XDM schema design, Data Prep transformations, identity namespace management.

fields.label: New skill to build
fields.text: Schema design: this is the highest-leverage new skill on the team, since a well-designed schema saves rework across every other role.

fields.label: Quick win
fields.text: Start schema design before any tag rebuild; it's the one artifact every other workstream depends on.

fields.label: Moving from
fields.text: Report suite and user management in the AA Admin Console.

fields.label: Moving to
fields.text: Sandboxes, Product Profiles, data governance labels, and consent management in Experience Platform.

fields.label: New skill to build
fields.text: Designing a sandbox strategy up front (how many, who owns which); retrofitting this later is expensive.

fields.label: Quick win
fields.text: Stand up a dev sandbox on day one so engineering can start schema work without touching production.
